statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Weekend venue closure with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail remains far below the block threshold while Stress stays elevated on hawkish rate repricing and Hormuz energy risk.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the session; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Quiet Sunday closure: hawkish payroll repricing and Hormuz escalation wait for a thin 22:00 UTC reopen into a US holiday
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape remains Friday September 4: ^NDX closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold, and VIX ended at 14.53. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% and the Nasdaq Composite 0.29% after the August employment report printed 162,000 payrolls against roughly 56,000 consensus, with June and July revised up a combined 55,000 and unemployment steady at 4.1%. That repricing lifted CME FedWatch odds of a 25bp hike at the September 15-16 FOMC to 58.4% from 49.4% a day earlier; H.15 still shows the September 3 readings of 2Y 4.34% and 10Y 4.77%. The pre-FOMC communications blackout began on September 5 and runs through September 17, which removes Fed-speaker headlines from the whole forecast window. On the geopolitical side, the picture is unchanged since Saturday evening: CENTCOM disabled two Iranian tankers and destroyed a third after IRGC ballistic-missile launches toward a US carrier and destroyer, and the IRGC then claimed strikes on three US-affiliated vessels and three tankers in Hormuz at 21:44 UTC. No verified new claim has appeared in the roughly thirteen hours since. Brent settled $96.28 and WTI $91.48, weekly gains of 7.6% and nearly 10%, with four commodity vessels transiting the strait on Thursday against a ten-day average near 15. That keeps Stress elevated, though the quiet overnight trims it a point. The strategy-relevant failure mode requires an observed no-retracement price path, and none exists: Friday closed mid-range, VIX stayed below 15, and internals were mixed with semiconductors firm while several megacaps fell. Tail therefore stays low and maps to EA_ON. Conditional risk concentrates in the 22:00-02:00 UTC reopen window, where the thinnest depth of the week meets a Monday Labor Day closure that removes the cash session normally available to absorb a weekend gap.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held flat at 4-5 with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress climbed from 38 during Saturday's European hours to a 57 peak around the Saturday evening tanker exchange, then oscillated between 52 and 56 across the remaining weekend closure. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover twelve further closed hours, the 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian and European session on a US Labor Day holiday. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band throughout, peaking at 18 in the reopen hour where two verified days of Hormuz escalation meet the thinnest depth of the week, then decaying toward 8 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 66 at the reopen on the combined rates and energy backdrop before unwinding toward 52. No US macro release falls inside the window and the Fed is in its pre-FOMC blackout; the next scheduled checkpoints are the NFIB survey on September 8, August PPI on September 10 and August CPI on September 11, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC.
